title: Pullback maps between computing cup resolutions
statement: Let $f:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $F,G$ be $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $f^*$ for tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and let $\tau:f^*(F\otimes G)\to f^*F\otimes f^*G$ be the canonical section-normalized comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. There exist computing resolution pairings $D$ for $F,G$ on $X$ and $E$ for $f^*F,f^*G$ on $X'$ [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data], and additive cochain maps $l,r,t$ between their respective left, right and target global section complexes. For every degree $n$, source global kernel cycle $z$ and target kernel cycle $z'$ whose underlying section is the appropriate degree map of $z$, the class of $z'$ is respectively $f^*[z]$, $f^*[z]$, or $H^n(\tau)f^*[z]$, using the canonical computing class maps and pullback [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. For every $p,q\geq0$ and global sections $a$ of $D_{\rm left}^p$, $b$ of $D_{\rm right}^q$, one has $t^{p+q}(D_{\rm pair}^{p,q}(a,b))=E_{\rm pair}^{p,q}(l^p(a),r^q(b))$. No cup product on cohomology is supplied as input and no cover or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Take the Godement models for F, G and F tensor G on X and for their pulled-back coefficients on X-prime. On each open V define the map of product-of-stalks objects by sending the coordinate at f(x-prime) through the stalk map of the adjunction unit, for each x-prime in f-inverse(V). The germ unit commutes with this map because both values are the germ of the pulled-back section. Evaluation commutes because both routes evaluate the same coordinate at x-prime. Iteration therefore commutes with every inserted unit and every evaluation, hence defines maps of the augmented cosimplicial resolutions. Taking alternating differentials and global sections gives additive cochain maps l, r and t. No tensor-pullback exactness is used.

source.place: cohomology-lemma-godement-resolution; coordinatewise extension to a morphism of ringed spaces

proof.text: For the two Godement models, use their coordinatewise tensor maps and Alexander--Whitney pairing. At each stalk the tensor-pullback comparison sends the image of a section tensor to the tensor of its two images. The cosimplicial maps from the first step commute with the front and back faces. In each bidegree the two routes thus evaluate to the same tensor coordinate. Composing the map for F tensor G with the map of its Godement resolution induced by the canonical tensor-pullback comparison gives the target map t and the displayed strict pairing equation. The signed Leibniz rule and degree-zero augmentation tensor equation equip the two models with pairings.

proof.text: All terms of the Godement resolutions are flasque, and their augmented stalk complexes contract by evaluation. Choose injective comparisons over the augmentations. Flasque acyclicity and the acyclic-resolution comparison criterion make these comparisons isomorphisms on global homology. They produce the computing pairings D and E.

source.place: cohomology-lemma-godement-resolution and computing flasque resolution comparison

proof.text: For each of the three coefficients, compare the augmented Godement map with the injective diagram defining the cohomology f-map. Resolve the pushforward of the target injective resolution by a complex of injectives. The source Godement complex has two maps into this complex: the source comparison followed by the injective f-map lift, and the Godement f-map followed by the pushforward target comparison and the injective replacement. They agree on the coefficient augmentation. The comparison homotopy for a quasi-isomorphic nonnegative augmentation and injective target makes the two maps homotopic. Global sections and homology identify them. Cancel the source and target computing homology isomorphisms and the pushforward-replacement homology isomorphism. This is precisely the defining formula of moduleCohomologyFMap under the two class maps. The third coefficient is the tensor unit followed by the tensor comparison, so target coefficient naturality supplies H(tensor comparison) after pullback. The concrete cycle projection commutes with the cochain maps by the homology-projection naturality, yielding the three class equations. Assemble the two pairings and three maps.

theorem moduleCup_pullback_resolution_maps (X X' : Scheme.{v}) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (F G : X.Modules) :
    ∃ (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
      (E : CupResolutionPairing ((tensorPullback f).obj F) ((tensorPullback f).obj G))
      (l : ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace ⋙
        forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K ⟶
      ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace ⋙
        forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.left.K)
      (r : ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace ⋙
        forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K ⟶
      ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace ⋙
        forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.right.K)
      (t : ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace ⋙
        forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K ⟶
      ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace ⋙
        forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.target.K),
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.left.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        a'.val = l.f n a.val →
          E.left.class n a' =
            moduleCohomologyPullback f F n (D.left.class n a)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.right.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        b'.val = r.f n b.val →
          E.right.class n b' =
            moduleCohomologyPullback f G n (D.right.class n b)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.target.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c'.val = t.f n c.val →
          E.target.class n c' =
            (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X'.toRingedSpace n).map
              ((Classical.choose (module_pullback_tensor f)) F G).hom
              (moduleCohomologyPullback f (@id X.Modules (F ⊗ G)) n
                (D.target.class n c))) ∧
      (∀ (p q : ℕ) (a : Γ(D.left.K.X p, ⊤)) (b : Γ(D.right.K.X q, ⊤)),
        t.f (p + q) (D.pair p q ⊤ a b) =
          E.pair p q ⊤ (l.f p a) (r.f q b))
